question: Should this work be re-cut from current main as a narrowly scoped UI cleanup, or is the current branch intentionally meant to carry the unrelated integration changes?
rationale: The stated cleanup is bounded and well-evidenced, but the actual branch combines multiple compatibility-, security-, and automation-sensitive surfaces that cannot be attributed to the cleanup without maintainer intent.

options.title: Re-cut from current main
options.body: Create a replacement branch containing only the intended UI export, test-cleanup, and baseline changes, then rerun the focused proof.

options.title: Retain as integration branch
options.body: Explicitly redefine the PR scope and obtain full owner review and proof for every dependency, protocol, SDK, iOS, agent, documentation, and automation change.

options.title: Supersede after replacement
options.body: Keep this branch paused until the narrow replacement is available, then close this PR in favor of that reviewable branch.

recommendation.title: Re-cut from current main
recommendation.body: Create a replacement branch containing only the intended UI export, test-cleanup, and baseline changes, then rerun the focused proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The history connects this person to the dead-export ratchet and the current cleanup branch, making them the best available owner for the scope decision.
